trainer_product.name: QA Engineer Interview Trainer
trainer_product.description: Text-based interview trainer for Junior QA candidates. Practice answering common QA interview questions with structured AI evaluation.
trainer_product.tagline: Junior QA Interview Preparation with AI Evaluation
trainer_product.welcome_message: Welcome to the Junior QA Interview Trainer! Practice answering common interview questions, receive structured feedback, and improve your skills.

qa_self_presentation_v1.title: Tell Me About Yourself as a QA Candidate
qa_self_presentation_v1.goal: Evaluate the candidate's ability to present themselves professionally, structure their background, and articulate their motivation for pursuing a QA role.

step_prompts.self_presentation_step_1: Please introduce yourself. Tell us about your background, your journey into QA, your key skills, and why you are interested in this Junior QA Engineer position. Structure your answer clearly.

hints: Follow a structure: past experience, transition to QA, current skills, future goals.
Use a professional tone and relevant technical background.
Avoid overly generic answers that don't connect to the QA role.
Mention specific technologies, tools, or methodologies you have worked with.

context.company: Mid-size product company looking for a Junior QA Engineer to join a mobile and web application team.

qa_test_case_vs_checklist_v1.title: Test Case vs Checklist: Differences and Use Cases
qa_test_case_vs_checklist_v1.goal: Evaluate the candidate's understanding of test documentation: the difference between test cases and checklists, their structure, when to use each, and the trade-offs involved.

step_prompts.tcc_step_1: Explain the difference between a test case and a checklist in software testing. Compare their structure, when you would use each, their advantages and disadvantages, and give specific examples of each.

hints: Test cases are detailed with preconditions, steps, expected results.
Checklists are lightweight lists of items to verify, good for smoke tests.
Discuss trade-offs: detail vs speed, maintenance effort, reusability.
Give examples from real testing scenarios.

context.company: A product company transitioning from startup processes to more structured QA.

qa_bug_report_structure_v1.title: Bug Report Structure
qa_bug_report_structure_v1.goal: Evaluate the candidate's knowledge of proper bug report structure, including all required fields, severity vs priority classification, and best practices for writing clear reproduction steps.

step_prompts.bug_report_step_1: Describe the ideal structure of a bug report. What fields should it contain? Explain the difference between severity and priority, and walk me through how you would write clear steps to reproduce. Give examples of good and bad bug report practices.

hints: A complete bug report includes: title, description, environment, steps to reproduce, actual/expected result, severity, priority, attachments.
Severity = impact on the system, Priority = urgency for the business.
Steps to reproduce should be clear, numbered, self-contained.
Include environment details: OS, browser, device, app version.

context.company: E-commerce platform using JIRA. Team works with distributed developers across time zones.

qa_regression_vs_retest_v1.title: Regression Testing vs Retesting
qa_regression_vs_retest_v1.goal: Evaluate the candidate's ability to distinguish between regression testing and retesting, understand when each is applied, and explain their roles in the QA process with practical examples.

step_prompts.rvr_step_1: Explain the difference between regression testing and retesting. When do you perform each? Why is it important to distinguish between them? Provide real-world examples from your experience or typical project scenarios.

hints: Retesting = testing a specific bug fix to confirm it's resolved. Focused and targeted.
Regression testing = checking that recent changes haven't broken existing functionality. Broader scope.
Retesting comes before regression testing in a typical workflow.
Regression often uses automated suites or risk-based approaches.

context.company: A fintech company with frequent releases. Team regularly deals with bug fixes and new features.

qa_login_form_testing_v1.title: Login Form Testing Scenarios
qa_login_form_testing_v1.goal: Evaluate the candidate's ability to design comprehensive test scenarios for a login form, applying test design techniques, identifying edge cases, and structuring their test coverage logically.

step_prompts.login_step_1: You are testing a login form with email, password, submit button, 'Remember Me' checkbox, and a 'Forgot Password' link. Design a comprehensive set of test scenarios. Use test design techniques (equivalence partitioning, boundary value analysis) and cover positive cases, negative cases, edge cases, and security aspects. Structure your answer into logical groups.

hints: Positive scenarios + negative: invalid email format, wrong password, empty fields.
Edge cases: long email, Unicode, SQL injection, XSS, brute force, session timeout.
Security: password masking, HTTPS, tokens, CAPTCHA.
Structure by groups: functional, negative, security, UX.

context.company: A SaaS platform with 2 million active users is redesigning its login page.

interview_disclaimer.title: About the Interview Simulation
interview_disclaimer.text: This trainer simulates a Junior QA Engineer interview using AI for answer evaluation. Evaluation is based on predefined criteria and may not fully reflect a real human-led interview. Use the feedback to improve your skills, but keep in mind that real interviews may differ in format and requirements.
